title: Spezzatino di Vitello
subtitle: Italian veal stew with peas and white wine
excerpt: Spezzatino is an Italian word for a braised stew of meat cut into pieces. This veal version, made with white wine, soffritto, and peas added at the end, is one of the most widely made spring and summer stews in northern and central Italy. It is lighter than a winter beef braise and cooks in under an hour.
sourceNotes: Spezzatino di vitello is a standard of Italian home cooking, appearing in cookbooks from Pellegrino Artusi onwards. The dish is made throughout northern and central Italy, with regional variations using peas, carrots, or mushrooms. It is a lighter braise than southern Italian stews, relying on white wine rather than tomatoes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the peas. Add freshly cooked peas when reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves if made a day ahead and gently reheated.

content.text: Veal shoulder is the right cut for spezzatino: it has enough fat and collagen to braise without drying out, and it cooks faster than beef. Cut the meat into even 3 to 4 cm cubes and dry the pieces well before browning -- wet meat steams rather than browns. The peas go in only for the last 5 minutes.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a wide heavy pan over high heat. Season {{veal-shoulder}} veal with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Brown in batches, about 3 minutes per side, until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add {{onion}} onion, {{celery}} celery, and {{carrot}} carrot to the pan. Cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Return the veal to the pan. Add the hot {{chicken-stock}} stock and {{lemon}} lemon zest. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 35 minutes until the veal is tender.
Add {{peas-frozen}} peas and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in {{parsley-flat}} parsley. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve with mashed potato, polenta, or crusty bread.

items.symptom: The veal is tough after 35 minutes
items.cause: The heat was too high, causing the meat fibres to tighten rather than relax.
items.fix: Continue cooking at the lowest possible simmer, covered, for a further 20 minutes. Veal shoulder needs sustained gentle heat. If the sauce reduces too much, add a splash of stock.

content.text: Spezzatino is the everyday family braise of northern Italy. It appears at Sunday lunch across Lombardy, Veneto, and Emilia-Romagna. The spring version with peas is the most common. It is a lighter dish than the long winter braises of the south, and because it uses white wine rather than red, the sauce stays pale and clean. Pellegrino Artusi, whose 1891 cookbook is the foundation of unified Italian cooking, included several versions of spezzatino in La Scienza in Cucina.
